items.title: Identifying a Table Corresponding to a Line

sections.normalized_html: The graph shows a straight line in the coordinate plane. Write a table that gives three [MATH: x]-values and their corresponding [MATH: y]-values for points that lie on the line.
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/53ee86c224b49ae9e46304049868fd43]

The graph shows a straight line in the coordinate plane. Write a table that gives three [MATH: x]-values and their corresponding [MATH: y]-values for points that lie on the line.

sections.normalized_html:

  • For [MATH: (-2, 0)]: when [MATH: x = -2,] the corresponding [MATH: y]-value is [MATH: 0.]

Therefore, the table is:

[MATH: x]

[MATH: y]

[MATH: -2]

[MATH: -4]

items.title: Identifying a Table Corresponding to a Function

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: f(x) = 6x - 1]

For the linear function [MATH: f,] write a table that shows the corresponding values of [MATH: f(x)] for [MATH: x=-1,1,2]
sections.readable_text:
[MATH: f(x) = 6x - 1]

For the linear function [MATH: f,] write a table that shows the corresponding values of [MATH: f(x)] for [MATH: x=-1,1,2]

sections.normalized_html:
To write the table, substitute each [MATH: x] into [MATH: f(x) = 6x - 1.]

For [MATH: x = -1{:}] [MATH: f(− 1)|= 6(− 1) − 1; = − 6 − 1; = − 7]

For [MATH: x = 1{:}] [MATH: f(1)|= 6(1) − 1; = 6 − 1; = 5]

For [MATH: x = 2{:}] [MATH: f(2)|= 6(2) − 1; = 12 − 1; = 11]

Therefore, the table is the following:

[MATH: x]

[MATH: f(x)]

[MATH: -1]

[MATH: -7]

[MATH: 1]

[MATH: 5]

[MATH: 2]

[MATH: 11]

[MATH: 2]

[MATH: 15]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In this lesson, we'll practice constructing tables corresponding to linear relationships, whether shown graphically as lines, written as functions, or expressed as equations. Dealing with functions expressed in tabular form is a common theme of the math section of the SAT exam.

---

Item 2 — Example: Identifying a Table Corresponding to a Line

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/53ee86c224b49ae9e46304049868fd43]

The graph shows a straight line in the coordinate plane. Write a table that gives three [MATH: x]-values and their corresponding [MATH: y]-values for points that lie on the line.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
From the graph, we can see that the points [MATH: (-3, 2),] [MATH: (0, -4),] and [MATH: (-2, 0)] lie on the line.

Now, we’ll analyze each of these points in turn:

- For [MATH: (-3, 2)]: when [MATH: x = -3,] the corresponding [MATH: y]-value is [MATH: 2.]
- For [MATH: (0, -4)]: when [MATH: x = 0,] the corresponding [MATH: y]-value is [MATH: -4.]
- For [MATH: (-2, 0)]: when [MATH: x = -2,] the corresponding [MATH: y]-value is [MATH: 0.]

Therefore, the table is:

| [MATH: x] | [MATH: y] |
| [MATH: -3] | [MATH: 2] |
| [MATH: -2] | [MATH: 0] |
| [MATH: 0] | [MATH: -4] |
